newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Rugby Union-Australia offer dates for England test.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Rugby Union-Australia offer dates for England test.

text.p: Australia have offered two alternative dates for a proposed test against England at Twickenham at the end of 1996 in an effort to revive their proposed fixture, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Australian Rugby Union chief executive John O'Neill has suggested playing England on November 2 or November 16, The Australian newspaper reported.

The Wallabies orginally sought to play England on December 7 but their tour hosts -- The Four Home Unions Tour Committee -- refused the request because it involved scrapping an existing match against the Barbarians at Twickenham the same day.

The Committee said it was too late to re-arrange the traditional fixture with the Barbarians, a scratch side drawn principally from the ranks of the four home countries, because more than 30,000 tickets had already been sold.
Australia's latest proposal would involve the cancellation of one provincial tour match, which could be re-scheduled for December 4, the newspaper reported O'Neill as saying.
"Surely there is no reason for anyone to knock us back this time," O'Neill said.
Australia have already confirmed tests against Wales, Ireland and Scotland during the eight-week tour and want to add England to complete a grand slam of the four home countries.
The tour begins in October in Italy, where the Wallabies will play a one-off test against their hosts, before heading to Britain.
